title: Over the fifteen months tested the live settings lose on both symbols
detail: Each quarter was run eight times on raw ticks on a fresh $2,000 with the live unit auto-step, with only the loop's timing drawn at random. Median result per quarter, gold: Aug–Nov 2025 −$2,000; Nov 2025–Feb 2026 −$1,277; Feb–May 2026 −$2,000; May–Aug 2026 −$2,000; Aug–Nov 2026 −$351; 37 of 40 quarter-runs lost money and 27 ended with the account stopped out. BTC: Aug–Nov 2025 −$1,369; Nov 2025–Feb 2026 −$1,407; Feb–May 2026 −$286; May–Aug 2026 −$190; Aug–Nov 2026 +$282; 30 of 40 lost money and 0 were stopped out. Run as one continuous account from 13 Aug 2025, gold was stopped out on 14 Oct 2025, day 62 and BTC was stopped out on 6 Feb 2026, day 177. The three months you asked for (13 Aug–13 Nov 2026) are the best of the five for gold and the best of the five for BTC, so they flatter the strategy.

title: It wins small and often and loses big and rarely, and the rare losses decide the result
detail: Gold, 13 Aug–13 Nov 2026: 93.5% of 3,620 baskets won, and it needs 94.1% to break even, because the average win is +$2.22 and the average loss −$35.15 (one loss cancels 16 wins). The worst basket lost $1,821, as much as 821 average wins; the ten worst gave back 51% of everything the winners made. The quarter ended −$793. BTC, 13 Aug–13 Nov 2026: 81.7% of 2,608 baskets won, and it needs 79.7% to break even, because the average win is +$1.24 and the average loss −$4.84 (one loss cancels 4 wins). The worst basket lost $125, as much as 101 average wins; the ten worst gave back 23% of everything the winners made. The quarter ended +$316. A win rate above 80 or 90% says nothing by itself: what matters is the point or two between the win rate and the break-even rate (gold 0.6 short of it, BTC 2.0 above), and that is decided by a handful of baskets.

title: One run is one path: the same quarter ends up or down depending on which ticks the loop happens to poll
detail: Gold, 13 Aug–13 Nov 2026, same settings, same ticks, eight random loop timings: from −$2,000 to +$58 (median −$351); with no random delay −$793. BTC: from +$171 to +$356 (median +$282); no random delay +$316. The reason is the pay-off above: whether the bot is inside a basket when a sharp move starts depends on the second it entered, and one such basket outweighs a month of wins. Even at one fixed 0.01-lot unit the result of a gold quarter moved by $2,197 at the median, and by up to $3,516, with nothing changed but the loop timing. So no single backtest figure, and no single live month, tells you whether a setting is good; only the spread over many runs and many quarters does.

title: The ladder is not a ladder: the last three adds usually go in about two seconds apart, at one price
detail: Each add is released when the RSI of its timeframe is beyond 35 / 65, which is a level, not a new event. When the M15, H1 and H4 RSI are already there, the third, fourth and fifth add fire on consecutive passes of the loop. On gold 85–100% of those adds came within ten seconds of the previous one (median 2 s), $0.24–0.28 away from it; the median spread at its entries is $0.26 (the quarter's median quote spread was $0.24). So 26 of the 32 units of a full ladder are one clip at one price, not an average-down. Gold baskets that never added made +$4,251 in the quarter; baskets that added lost $5,040; the 40 that reached all six positions account for −$1,839, with an average loss of $567 when they lost. BTC shows the same timing (79–98% within ten seconds): +$1,191 without adds, −$874 with.

title: The only loss exit watches momentum pivots, not price or money, and nothing stands behind it
detail: A losing basket is closed when the M15 RSI / MACD pivot score turns against it. In a steady adverse move that score stays neutral or supportive. The worst gold basket of the quarter was a BUY of 0.64 lots opened on 22 Oct 2026 at 4,037.27: it was held 7.3 hours while price moved $28.45 against its average entry and was closed at −$1,821. 67% of gold's losing baskets were closed within 10% of the worst point they ever showed, 28% had been in profit before, and one basket that ended as a winner had been $1,003 under water on the way. There is no price stop, no time stop and no equity stop, and the stop sent to the broker is not a stop (see the live-code findings).

title: The entry signal says nothing about where price goes next
detail: An entry needs the M15 RSI vote and the M15 MACD vote to agree. Both are measured from the last pivot of their indicator, so both are votes to fade the last extreme: over the fifteen months the MACD vote pointed against its own signal-line trend on 80% of gold's M15 bars (79% for BTC), and 88% of RSI up-votes came after an oversold low. Tested on every closed M15 bar with the live indicator code: after both votes pointed up, gold was higher four bars later 50.8% of the time, against 50.8% for any bar; after both pointed down it was lower 49.9% of the time, against 49.2%. BTC: 51.5% against 50.0%, and 50.8% against 50.0%. That is a coin flip. The wins come from the target being close and the stop being absent, not from the signal knowing direction, which is why the timeframes the signal is read on cannot fix the result.

title: The spread takes a large share of what the winners make
detail: Gold paid $2,945 of spread in the quarter, 39% of the winners' gross profit, on 39 baskets a day; before spread the closed baskets net +$2,157, after it −$788 (−$793 with the basket still open at the end). BTC paid $728 (28% of the winners' gross). A $1 target on 0.01 lot is a $1 move in gold against a median spread at entry of $0.26. The spread was not the same in every quarter (see the hold-out section), and the strategy's result moves with it.

title: The unit auto-step raises the stake after a good run and the next loss is taken at the larger size
detail: The unit is floor(balance / 2,500) + 1, re-derived whenever the account is flat. In the gold quarter: unit 1: 1,607 baskets, +$124 (worst −$295); unit 2: 2,013 baskets, −$912 (worst −$1,821). The account crossed $2,500 on small wins at one unit and gave it back at two. Because the target also scales with the unit while the worst case of a basket has no limit, stepping up multiplies the tail, not the edge.

title: No choice of timeframes makes it pay: settings that look good on one period do not hold on another
detail: 432 combinations of OPEN and FORCE-CLOSE timeframes were run on five quarters (one fixed 0.01-lot unit; "wiped" replays the baskets on a real $2,000 account with the bot's lot sizing). Gold: 12 of 432 settings were profitable in all three analysed quarters without wiping a $2,000 account. On the two hold-out quarters 0% of those were profitable in both and 75% wiped the account in one (mean −$1,164 a quarter), against 6% and 75% (mean −$1,245) for all settings; rank correlation between the two periods +0.30. BTC: 25 of 432 settings were profitable in all three analysed quarters without wiping a $2,000 account. On the two hold-out quarters 0% of those were profitable in both and 80% wiped the account in one (mean −$1,423 a quarter), against 0% and 71% (mean −$1,706) for all settings; rank correlation between the two periods +0.37. No gold setting was profitable in all five quarters without wiping the account. No BTC setting was profitable in all five quarters without wiping the account. Averaged over all five quarters every timeframe loses. As an OPEN timeframe slower loses less: strictly in order on BTC, on gold with M30 out of line. As FORCE-CLOSE, gold's H4 and H1 lose least but M30 loses more than M15 and M5; on BTC there is no clear order. Mean net per quarter, gold: FORCE-CLOSE on H4 −$271, H1 −$429, M30 −$1,723, M15 −$1,132, M5 −$1,416, M1 −$2,159; OPEN containing H4 −$664, H1 −$888, M15 −$910, M30 −$1,280, M5 −$1,450, M1 −$1,738. BTC: FORCE-CLOSE on H4 −$606, H1 −$1,185, M30 −$696, M15 −$617, M5 −$1,030, M1 −$1,655; OPEN containing H4 −$723, H1 −$794, M30 −$869, M15 −$927, M5 −$1,053, M1 −$1,298. The live setting (OPEN H1+M15, FORCE-CLOSE M15) on gold: Aug–Nov 2025 −$2,461, Nov 2025–Feb 2026 +$854, Feb–May 2026 −$2,299, May–Aug 2026 −$2,356, Aug–Nov 2026 +$296. Keep in mind that each cell is a single path whose result moves by about $2,200 a quarter on gold (up to $3,500) and a few hundred dollars on BTC with the loop timing alone.

title: Removing the ladder cuts the worst loss many times over; nothing tested makes the live timeframes reliably profitable
detail: Each what-if changes one rule, or one small package of rules, and leaves the rest live (one fixed unit, three 2026 quarters, single paths). Gold: live settings: −$4,359 over three quarters, worst basket −$1,687, account wiped; no ladder: −$2,321 over three quarters, worst basket −$217; ladder: adds >= $3 apart: −$2,701 over three quarters, worst basket −$1,243, account wiped; stop: $20 per unit: −$5,107 over three quarters, worst basket −$166, account wiped; no ladder + stop $10: −$2,807 over three quarters, worst basket −$58; cooldown 30 min: −$2,928 over three quarters, worst basket −$1,687, account wiped; signals on closed bars: −$6,829 over three quarters, worst basket −$2,545, account wiped. BTC: live settings: −$340 over three quarters, worst basket −$484; no ladder: −$248 over three quarters, worst basket −$26; ladder: adds >= $300 apart: −$147 over three quarters, worst basket −$84; stop: $20 per unit: −$2,074 over three quarters, worst basket −$45; no ladder + stop $10: −$296 over three quarters, worst basket −$13; cooldown 30 min: −$966 over three quarters, worst basket −$484; signals on closed bars: −$904 over three quarters, worst basket −$377. A stop alone turns a rare large loss into frequent medium ones; the ladder is what makes the large loss large. These are directions to test on a demo account, not settings to deploy. Spacing the ladder cut the worst loss many times over on BTC but only by about a quarter on gold.

title: What does hold up on data it was never fitted to: a with-trend design with a real stop and no ladder (gold)
detail: Designs were chosen on 13 Aug 2025 – 13 Nov 2026 and Jan 2024 – Jun 2025, frozen, and then run once on Feb – Dec 2023 (three quarters and one two-month block), which had played no part in any choice (every tick, eight loop timings per quarter, a real $2,000 account with the bot's unit rule). V3-lite, entries only with the H1 trend (H1 MACD signal line), H1 votes with M15 agreement, stop and target 8 H1-volatility units on the whole basket, no ladder, a 12 h pause after a losing basket, made +$106 per block on gold in 2023 with no losing run of 32, and +$152 a quarter with none of 48 losing in 2024 – mid 2025; the live settings lost $666 and $675 a quarter there. On BTC no design made money reliably: V3-lite +$7 a quarter in 2023, the live settings lost $1,194. About 1,200 designs were tried, so the 2023 figure is the honest one; the edge is small (gold about +$4 a basket). See IMPROVEMENT.md.

title: Support and resistance, and the other ways to recover a losing position, do not add an edge
detail: Two independent studies of H1, H4 and D1 levels (swing highs and lows, the previous day's and week's high and low, round numbers): price turned at the levels no more often than at placebo prices, and no bounce rule made money after the spread in either period. A few gold breakout and retest rules with the trend were slightly positive in both, but they were found after the fact and did no better than placebo levels in 2025-26. Forty-two position-management mechanisms on the same 32,553 entries (averaging down with a budget, averaging up, break-even and trailing stops, scale-out, hedge lock, zone recovery, stop-and-reverse, martingale): none raised the expectancy; they only change how the result is distributed. A ladder with equal lots, at most two adds and a hard $60 budget, flat over every market closure, never lost more than $60 (held over closures, up to −$222 on gold), and earned no more than not adding. A hedge lock unlocked on the next signal pays exactly what closing and re-entering pays; a lock that is simply closed later costs one spread more than a stop. Reports: backtest_results/improve/.
